rules.product: a file under aisef2/: every target of that module (the module digest is whole-file); every target of a module that imports it from aisef2 (its enum members are generator input); every target whose kill tests' closure holds it (code outside tests/: reported by the proof, not counted)
rules.kill_file: in a V2.1 target's kill set at base or head: that target
rules.kill_closure: in the closure of a target's kill files (s2_mutation_record.closure, at base or head) without being one: that target; under tests/ the proof counts it, elsewhere it reports it
rules.harness: validation/v2/mutation.py, execution_order.py, owned_run.py, cleanup_authority.py and their closure: every V2.1 target, stated as such in the file's row and in every target's row; the proof's rules do not bind the runner's code
rules.data: a file inside mutation.COPY outside the harness is data to every target it is not the module of; per kill file of such a target whose closure does not hold it, measured: read when the measured read-set says so (opened or looked up, or a directory above it listed), not read when it omits it and the file exists at head, else not measured; not measured: may read when found statically in a file of that closure inside COPY (no other file is in the runner's tree), tests/ or not, at base or head — the whole path in its text; its path split into consecutive parts, each a whole string constant, from the repository root or a directory above that file; a parent directory of two components or more and the rest or the basename; or the file lists a directory (a call of glob, iglob, rglob, iterdir, listdir, scandir, walk or fwalk whose receiver and arguments name it: their string constants joined in source order up to the first part with *, ? or [, from the root or a directory above that file) that is the parent directory, or any directory above when it lists recursively (rglob, walk, fwalk, a ** pattern) — and not measured all the same
rules.copy_data: inside COPY, read by <kill files> (read_set.read_by: measured — their targets' base results are no ground at head: re-measure them (counts.data_read) —, or found statically: they may read it, and are not measured): their targets; outside the proof's rules
rules.copy_unmeasured: inside COPY, read-set not measured (found statically or not): for every target with such a kill file, its base result stands only PROVISIONALLY until a measured read-set clears the file; read_set.provisional counts them (provisional_except: the targets of the build it does not hold)
rules.copy_unread: inside COPY and not read by any kill file the other rules leave open (measured read-set): no target
rules.code: a .py or .sh file or a #! script that no rule above ties to a target by code (not under aisef2/, no kill file, in no kill closure, not the harness); inside COPY it is data as well
rules.evidence/doc: none of the above (outside COPY, not code): no target
rules.verdict: v21_mutation_record.proof for a result measured at base, at head (re-implemented per commit; proof.criteria_sha256 is the one it was derived beside)
rules.records: manifest: a new revision when a target, a kill set or a target module changed, or a file it binds by sha256 differs at head; T0: every (module, null mutant, kill file) pair a head target needs with no PASS row in the manifest's T0 record, or whose kill file changed since the sweep, and that base did not already need; execution order: kill sets, targets, null mutants, the T0 pairs, execution_order.py or the T0 record changed; Q0: checker_calibration.py, a validation/v2 module, a checker's source or a known-bad fixture changed
